raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

When a client sends an image the multimodal processor refuses (a PNG whose IDAT checksum is wrong, a JPEG truncated mid-scan, a format the decoder does not support), the Python server raises `ValueError` from its processor and `http_server` answers 400 with the processor's message. The Rust server mapped every `Error::Encode` to `CoreError::Internal`, so the same request answered 500 with `encode failed: <message>`. A 500 for bad client input reads as a server fault to routers and alerting, and a disaggregated pair whose prefill and decode run different frontends answers the same request with different status classes.

## Modifications

- `MmProcessor::process` returns `Result<MmProcessOutput, MediaError>` instead of `Result<_, String>`, the type the `fetch_media` hook already uses. `Client` is what Python's processor raises as `ValueError` (refused media, a placeholder matching no item); `Server` is `RuntimeError` and any other exception. `QwenMmProcessor` maps the driver's failure to `Client` and a failed output encode to `Server`.
- `Error::Encode` carries the `MediaError`. Admission (`prepare_generations`) and the MM worker's failure (`translate_runtime_error`) both map it through one `From<MediaError> for CoreError`: `Client` is a 400, or an SSE error event with code 400 on a stream, with the processor's own message and no `encode failed: ` prefix; `Server` stays a 500. Only `Encode(Server)` counts as a server fault.
- The worker's own faults stay 500s: a malformed processor result, a failed `finalize` or a feature buffer that cannot be placed fail as `Error::Internal`.
- `payload.rs` classifies its errors: a malformed data URL, bare base64 or a blown byte budget is `Client`; a prefetch that disagrees with the walk is `Server`.
- Test processors return `MediaError`; `worker_returns_request_with_fsm_advanced` covers refused, failing and malformed processors, and a new runtime test `refused_media_is_a_bad_request` drives `/generate` unary and streaming through a refusing and a failing processor and checks the status, the code and the message.

Files: `rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/core/{error,prefetch}.rs`, `api_server/handlers/{generate,handle}.rs`, `multi_modality/{payload,worker}.rs`, `tokenizer_manager/to_scheduler_tests.rs`, `utils/{error,runtime}.rs`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model forward or kernel code changes. Unit coverage in `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server` on this branch (413 tests pass; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean):

- `runtime::tests::refused_media_is_a_bad_request`: through a running runtime, a processor returning `MediaError::Client("image decode failed: CRC error")` answers `/generate` with 400 and `{"message":"image decode failed: CRC error","code":400}`, and on a stream a 200 whose error event carries code 400; `MediaError::Server(...)` answers 500 / code 500.
- `worker::tests::worker_returns_request_with_fsm_advanced`: a refusing processor fails the request as `Encode(Client)` (not a server fault); a failing processor and a malformed result fail it as a server fault.
- `payload::tests::*` assert the class of each error: unsupported modality, no image sources and byte-budget overruns are `Client`; a missing prefetch entry is `Server`.
- `to_scheduler_tests::mm_failure_rejects_returned_request` keeps covering the rejection path with an `Encode(Client)` error.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: an enum variant in place of a `String` on the error path only.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations): no user-facing flag changes.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed): not applicable.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -3,6 +3,8 @@
 
 use thiserror::Error;
 
+use crate::multi_modality::worker::MediaError;
+
 // Some variants are emitted only once their stage matures (real validation,
 // the deferred Encoder, HF detok). They are part of the stable error surface.
 #[allow(dead_code)]
@@ -14,8 +16,11 @@ pub enum Error {
     #[error("tokenize failed: {0}")]
     Tokenize(String),
 
+    /// The multimodal processor failed the request, keeping Python's status
+    /// class: refused media (an undecodable image, a placeholder that matches
+    /// no item, ...) is the client's, anything else the server's.
     #[error("encode failed: {0}")]
-    Encode(String),
+    Encode(MediaError),
 
     #[error("detokenize failed: {0}")]
     Detokenize(String),
@@ -42,7 +47,7 @@ impl Error {
         matches!(
             self,
             Error::Tokenize(_)
-                | Error::Encode(_)
+                | Error::Encode(MediaError::Server(_))
                 | Error::Detokenize(_)
                 | Error::Codec(_)
                 | Error::Internal(_)
